clue.text: Actual report tough policeman gets by end of day

parts.note: tough means hard, as in a hard man
a cop is an informal word for a policeman

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so take the last letter of day

explanation.surface: A hard-boiled detective files a genuine account of his shift before the day is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed paper version of a document is the tangible, real record, as opposed to one held only on screen.

clue.text: Part of match that's suitable for me?

definitions.text: Part of match that's suitable for me?

parts.words: Part of match that's suitable for me?
parts.note: the interval in a football match, read as 'half of the word time', which is exactly the two letters m and e

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which stage of a game would suit them best.
explanation.walkthrough: The break between the two halves of a match is its literal sense; the cryptic sense notes that ME is the second half of the word TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval between the two halves of a football or rugby game bears this name.

clue.text: One dodges restoring engine noise

indicators.note: something that dodges slips out of the way, so the letter for one leaves the word

parts.note: restoring someone to life is reviving them
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone avoids the work of fixing a car engine that is making a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodges' tells you I (one) gets out of REVIVING, leaving the gerund of the verb for gunning an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing a motor so it roars at high speed is the sound a driver makes when pumping the accelerator.

clue.text: Breaking news from Belfast?

definitions.meaning: breaking, as of a voice or a plate
in Ireland the word (also spelt craic) means gossip, news and lively chat

explanation.surface: A newsreader announces breaking news from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland, where this word (Irish craic) means chat or the latest gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a break, and in Irish English the same word means gossip or the latest talk.

clue.text: Attractive quality that could make Phi cultured

indicators.note: the letters of the next two words could be made into a new word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a Greek letter might become refined and charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' signals rearranging PHI CULTURED into a literary word for physical beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: This rather formal word means great physical beauty, the quality of being good-looking.

clue.text: Country where one's about to reach the shore

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I, with 's as is
re is a Latin word for about or concerning
to land a boat is to reach the shore

explanation.surface: A sailor names the country where they are about to come ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republic on the western island of the British Isles is a nation, with Dublin its capital.

clue.text: Area of activity that's the result of the bottle?

definitions.meaning: a place where something flourishes or is intensely active, as in a centre of intrigue
a hot-water bottle leaves a warmed bed behind it

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a busy scene came about from too much drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bottle' suggests drink, but the second reading is a hot-water bottle warming the sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where something such as crime or dissent thrives, and literally a warmed bed.

clue.text: Nothing shown by British in beer is attractive

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis

indicators.note: in tells you one piece sits inside another here

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A Brit drinking beer proves to be a charmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone easy to be fond of is endearing and appealing.

clue.text: Customer's position requiring note in court

definitions.note: read as customer is, with the 's as a link to the wordplay

indicators.note: in tells you the next pieces are set inside the abbreviation

parts.note: the lie of something is its position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: A customer finds himself having to put a note into the legal system.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who buys goods or services from a professional or business is a patron or buyer.

clue.text: Consider recipient of honour no good after reverse

indicators.note: after being put into reverse, the remaining letters are read from back to front
no good means the letter for good is lost from the word

parts.note: a knight receives a knighthood, an honour from the monarch

explanation.surface: A knighted person is urged to think again after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G (good) from KNIGHT to give KNIHT, which 'after reverse' turns backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or reflect on something is to weigh it up in the mind.

clue.text: Retreat? Man leading marines-it will take a long time'

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
RM stands for Royal Marines
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: A man in charge of a troop of marines says the job will take forever.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote dwelling where a recluse lives apart from the world is a secluded refuge.

clue.text: Study 50% complete, new students taking time for drinks, etc

indicators.note: a job only half complete has done just its first half, so take the first two of the four letters

parts.note: to study a subject is to read it, as at university
freshmen are new students in their first year

explanation.surface: Half-way through revision, a group of first-years take a break for drinks and snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: READ is a British way of saying study a subject at university; only its first half, RE, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Food and drink offered to revive people, as at a party or interval, goes by this word.

clue.text: When working, I am deflecting — electric current, say

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put into a new working order

explanation.surface: A machine announces that, once switched on, it diverts an electrical flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When working' tells you to rearrange I AM DEFLECTING; the definition by example works because every electric current creates this around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A current flowing in a wire generates a region of magnetic force, so it is one way to produce this.

clue.text: Hear tune varied round end of dreary Weber opera

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the extra letter
a tune that is varied is reworked, so its letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter, so take the last letter of dreary

explanation.surface: A listener notes a tune changing around a dull passage in a German romantic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges HEAR TUNE, and 'round' puts it around Y, the 'end of dreary'. Carl Maria von Weber wrote this 1823 opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Weber's grand romantic opera of 1823, set in medieval France, bears this title.

clue.text: Catholic liturgy's appearance after upset in rules

parts.note: a rite is a liturgy or form of worship, with 's as is

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is an appearance or manner

explanation.surface: A church service's look is overturned for breaking the regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards or tests by which things are judged serve as principles.

clue.text: A lot of money given to bank clerk, I predict

parts.note: a fortune is a large sum of money
a teller is a clerk who handles cash in a bank

explanation.surface: Someone hands a bank cashier a lot of cash and makes a prophecy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description of oneself: a person who says 'I predict' is a seer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clairvoyant who foresees people's futures would naturally say these words.

clue.text: Upset referee intended to send one off — much anger?

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads bottom to top
to send off is to dismiss, so a letter is removed from the word
with send, off tells you the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: meant means intended
A is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A referee in turmoil means to dismiss a player amid fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns REF into FER; 'send ... off' removes A (one) from MEANT to give MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of agitation or unrest, a seething turmoil, can be a great deal of rage.

clue.text: Dish Angela's cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Angela has prepared a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges ANGELAS (the apostrophe adds no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Layered pasta baked with sauce is an Italian oven-baked meal.

clue.text: One politician's legislation producing effect

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament, with 's as is
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A single politician's law produces results.
explanation.definitionFit: A marked influence or consequence is a force or result.

clue.text: Exotic city libertine dropped in bog

indicators.note: something dropped in is put inside another word

parts.note: a marsh is a bog
a rake is a dissolute man or libertine

explanation.surface: A womaniser falls into a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan city is a famous destination, its souks and medina a byword for the far-flung.

clue.text: Rota, we hear, is a composer

indicators.note: we hear tells you the word is chosen for its sound

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a duty schedule sounds like a music maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Nino Rota was also a composer, which makes 'composer' look as if it defines 'Rota'.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz, the Hungarian Romantic pianist, wrote the Hungarian Rhapsodies.

clue.text: Weapon: ineffectual blow's no good

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is dropped from the word

parts.note: a glancing blow strikes obliquely without full force, with 's as is

explanation.surface: A fighter laments that a feeble strike is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A long spear carried by a mounted knight is an arm used in battle and jousting.

clue.text: Spies finding information among old servicewomen

indicators.note: among means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: the ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the women's branch of the British Army until 1949
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Secret operatives get information from retired women soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret operatives or undercover operatives are intelligence officers.

clue.text: Green tea to be brewed for youngster

indicators.note: brewing mixes things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pot of green tea is set to brew for a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person aged thirteen to nineteen is an adolescent.

clue.text: Hat displaying bird on a good deal of greenery

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

indicators.note: a good deal of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: fern is green foliage

explanation.surface: A small bird perched on leafy plants is put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: TITFER is British slang for a hat, from cockney rhyming slang 'tit for tat' = hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This cockney slang term for headgear comes from rhyming slang.

clue.text: Greek character seen around rocky Crete and so on

indicators.note: around means the letters go round the rearranged word

parts.note: eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A Greek figure is spotted touring the rocky island of Crete, among other places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' signals the island's name being shaken up, and 'around' has the Greek letter split to enclose the result; 'seen' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'and the rest', used to end a list.
